arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 20 June 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence.

arrival_year.note: THE MAN'S OWN RECOLLECTION, NOT A CONTEMPORARY RECORD. He registered at the Calumet Club on the roll of 1879 and gave 1835, April, as his date of coming to Chicago — forty-four years after the fact. The roll's own `arrival_year_basis` says it dates the claim and does not prove it, so the year is carried at `inferred` and the household's `arrival` block keeps the bound the contemporary evidence sets.

origin.note: A BIRTHPLACE, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME CLAIM. The Calumet Club roll of 1879 gives “New York.” as where this man was BORN; this field asks where the household came FROM, and a generation that moved west in stages frequently did not come from the state it was born in. It is carried as the best statement of origin the sources make about this household and not as a last residence.

THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 20 June 1835 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1). FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Tuthill King” (f1839_v0371, printed page 43, ward 2, voting for John H. Kinzie). What a match may carry, and it is short: that the man was in Chicago on 2 May 1837 and in that ward. It is written as 1837 evidence with describes_date 1837-05-02, never as an 1835 fact, and the person's grade does not move on this alone. Under the ratified ladder a second contemporary source is what lifts projected_resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE, not about July 1835. The ward is a location in the CITY of 1837, whose six wards are drawn on printed page 46; it is not a location in the town of 1835 and does not place a house. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: Surname 'King' folds to the same string as the 1837 entry's, and the given name of both begins T. (data/research/directories/fergus_1839_election_crosswalk_1835.json and fergus_1839_register_crosswalk_1835.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a poll twenty-two months after the scene date — or a register four years after it — is a second source about CONTINUED RESIDENCE rather than about July 1835. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “KING TUTHILL”, 1836-06-29: 2 lots in the platted town — the N2 of lot 5 of block 9 in the town the register codes CHI (N2L5BL9CHI, as printed); the S2 of lot 5 of block 9 in the town the register codes CHIV (S2L5BL9CHIV, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $2620.00 (ls1290, ls1291). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $2620.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: KING TUTHILL matches Tuthill King: the forename names Tuthill King of the 7 people of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. OLD SETTLERS, 1879 — A DATE THIS MAN GAVE FOR HIMSELF, AND STILL NOT A FACT ABOUT 1835. The Calumet Club's FIRST reception to the settlers of Chicago prior to 1840, 27 May 1879, printed its register in the proceedings (Early Chicago, Chicago, 1879, pages 84-90), and this man's entry reads “King, Tuthill, | 1835, April, | New York. | 75 | Chicago.” — name, his own date of arrival, his birthplace, his age and his 1879 post-office address, in the register's five columns. The date of arrival is HIS RECOLLECTION, set down forty to sixty years after the event; the address is where he lived in 1879 and is never read as an 1835 residence. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a later recollection corroborates, enriches and dates and cannot lift a rung by itself, so this record's GRADE IS UNCHANGED by it: T-0513 consolidates the identity and T-0515 regrades. Identity by rule OS1 — surname and spelled-out forename agree, one bearer (data/research/old_settlers/crosswalk.json).

THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

directories.note: LATER EVIDENCE, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. A Chicago directory of 1839, 1843 or 1844 meets somebody of this name and this pass records what it prints. Under the ratified ladder a directory read after 1835 can corroborate that a person attested here was still in Chicago and can print a trade or a street the 1835 record never had; on its own it makes nobody a resident of 1835. Nothing on this person's 1835 record was regraded, moved, dated or given an occupation by this entry. WHAT THIS PASS RULED ONTO THIS HOUSEHOLD, named so the ruling can be found again: each volume below is followed by the printed entries it set against this person and the status the crosswalk ruled them at — a single entry carries what its own `could_carry` declares, and an ambiguous or contested match carries nothing and is shown so that the silence is legible. king_tuthill, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 — f1839_e0858 (a single entry); king_tuthill, Fergus's Chicago directory of 1843 — f1843_e1494 (a single entry); king_tuthill, Norris's Chicago directory of 1844 — n1844_e1024 (a single entry).

back_projection.note: A LATER ADDRESS, READ BACKWARDS 4 YEARS. The door is not an 1835 reading: Fergus's Chicago directory of 1839 printed it in 1839, and this pass carries it back to the scene date because the 1835 record attests a trade for this person and nothing in the corpus places it better. What is claimed is the street face and nothing narrower — no lot, no roof, no door count — and the grade is `reconstructed`, which is this dataset's word for a figure the reconstruction supplies rather than a source. Lake Street stands in 1835 under that name and in that place. The directory gives a street and nothing this pass can resolve narrower, so the placement is the FACE — the unit the owner's ruling of 2026-08-29 says a street name constrains — and no roof is dealt. The rule this stands on is docs/ADDRESS-BACK-PROJECTION.md and the liberty is L218; a reader who thinks 4 years is too far to carry a shop should read the grade as the disagreement being invited.
